nodes.title: A game sighting counts toward naming a mix-up only on a discriminating level: one on which the mix-up and every habit child in the battery predict different acts. kon/place vertex-off: two levels whose base directions differ by 45 degrees or more, the offset the same in the protractor's frame and different on the board (a fixed finger offset is not named). kon/name say: the generator serves levels where reading across in either direction puts the vertex in the middle; H3 confirms. Measure and draw serve at least one acute and one anticlockwise angle by a session's fourth level. Reverse: no discriminating level can be built for a mix-up in a mode, then it is not named from that mode.

Games' habit battery (tests/_habit-children.mjs, claude/r7-games 3731cca54) run through served sessions before any rule change: every fade x pL (none, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9) x 8 door sequences, four levels. Reproduced: stambh/tally '16 every time' 0.19 and 'what I typed last time' 0.23 at fade 1 (full sweep); kon/place a key served twice in about 65% of measure sessions, 'first key one row low' 0.22 at fade 2, '75 every level' 0.5 at fade 2; kon/name say the same swap 1.0, reading across 1.0, one random slip 0.15. New: a fixed drop 16 to 32 px above the vertex named vertex-off 0.94 (measure), 0.89 (draw). The judge's tally 0.95 was a model's figure, not the served path's.

On the levels served today a habit and a mix-up can be the same act on every level (a finger that lands above the vertex and the edge-on-vertex belief; reading letters across and vertex-first), because the generator serves almost only obtuse angles opening clockwise and no say level where reading across puts the vertex in the middle. 'Two different acts' cannot separate them; only a level on which they predict different acts can.
